name: code-commandments
title: Code Commandments
description: The static code checker judges the codebase, its hooks run inside the journal, and every rule and language is a switch in its settings

curl.hint: curl fetches the checker's release binary into the plugin's own folder

sha256sum.hint: sha256sum or shasum checks the fetched binary against its release's SHA256SUMS

setup.name: Fetch the checker's release binary, checked against its SHA256SUMS
Write the chosen switches into config.json
Check for sins, on demand
setup.run: journal check create "Check for sins" --set command=".journal/plugins/code-commandments/bin/commandments-release judge" --set every=0 --set failure="Code Commandments found {summary}"

folders_judged.title: Folders to check
folders_judged.help: One folder per line, from the project root. Empty, the config keeps the folders it names.

folders_skipped.title: Folders to leave out
folders_skipped.help: One folder per line, never read or reported, such as generated code. This list is what the config leaves out.

sin_blank-string-default.title: BlankStringDefault
sin_blank-string-default.help: `string $x = ''` standing in for absence — then asked `$x === ''`

sin_blank-string-on-the-wire.title: BlankStringOnTheWire
sin_blank-string-on-the-wire.help: A `string` field sent over the wire whose TypeScript reader has to check `=== ''` to mean "missing" — only that reader knows the blank stands for absence.

sin_cancelled-coalesce.title: CancelledCoalesce
sin_cancelled-coalesce.help: `??` cancelled by the comparison it sits in — `($x ?? '') !== ''`

sin_conditional-array-spread.title: ConditionalArraySpread
sin_conditional-array-spread.help: An array built by spreading a conditional element — `...($x ? ['k' => $x] : [])` or `array_merge($base, $cond ? [...] : [])` — a ternary-and-empty-array trick that really just means "include this when the value is present."

sin_de-nulled-finder.title: DeNulledFinder
sin_de-nulled-finder.help: A finder that returns `null` for both "missing" and "broken" instead of throwing — the kind of `?T` finder whose callers all end up de-nulling it.

sin_erased-null-object.title: ErasedNullObject
sin_erased-null-object.help: A blank-rendering Null Object written into a `string` slot — coerced back to `''`

sin_nullable-callback.title: NullableCallback
sin_nullable-callback.help: Nullable callback normalised in the body instead of a Null Object default

sin_option-as-nullable.title: OptionAsNullable
sin_option-as-nullable.help: `Option<T>` used as if it were nullable — `?Option`, `Option | null`, `unwrapOr(null)`

sin_flag-argument.title: FlagArgument
sin_flag-argument.help: a method whose whole body branches on a `bool` parameter — or on whether a nullable one was given — two methods sharing one name

sin_member-after-method.title: MemberAfterMethod
sin_member-after-method.help: A trait use, constant, property, property hook, or enum case declared below a method — so the reader only meets that state after seeing the behaviour that uses it.

sin_member-out-of-order.title: MemberOutOfOrder
sin_member-out-of-order.help: A declaration in the head of a class that arrives after something belonging below it — a constant under a property, a public field under a private one, a hook above the fields it reads

sin_namespace-cycle.title: NamespaceCycle
sin_namespace-cycle.help: two namespaces that reference each other — neither can be read, tested or moved alone

sin_namespace-dependency.title: NamespaceDependency
sin_namespace-dependency.help: a declared layer references a layer it may not use (the arrow points back up)

sin_archaeology-comment.title: ArchaeologyComment
sin_archaeology-comment.help: History/archaeology comments ("formerly / used to be / refactored / no longer an X / was extracted")

sin_ceremony-docblock.title: CeremonyDocblock
sin_ceremony-docblock.help: Docblock that only restates the typed signature (`@param Type $x`, no description)

sin_dangling-doc-reference.title: DanglingDocReference
sin_dangling-doc-reference.help: A docblock `{@see}`/`{@link}` cross-references a FIRST-PARTY class that does not exist in the codebase — documentation pointing at a name that was renamed or removed, never at what the code actually is

sin_inline-docblock.title: InlineDocblock
sin_inline-docblock.help: A docblock whose delimiter shares a line with its text — a one-liner, or a block that opens or closes next to content

sin_negative-space-comment.title: NegativeSpaceComment
sin_negative-space-comment.help: A comment defending the code against a strawman ("not random", "no magic", "not a coincidence", "not dead code")

sin_restated-comment.title: RestatedComment
sin_restated-comment.help: An inline comment that only spells the statement below it back in prose ("// save the order" over `$this->orders->save($order)`)

sin_stacked-docblock.title: StackedDocblock
sin_stacked-docblock.help: Two or more docblocks stacked on one declaration — PHP reads only the last, so the ones above it are documentation nobody sees

sin_const-class-enum.title: ConstClassEnum
sin_const-class-enum.help: A class of 2+ scalar `const`s and nothing else — a closed set hand-rolled as constants instead of a native enum

sin_enum-case-or-chain.title: EnumCaseOrChain
sin_enum-case-or-chain.help: `$x === Enum::A || $x === Enum::B` — a hand-rolled case-group test

sin_enum-value-match.title: EnumValueMatch
sin_enum-value-match.help: A `match`/`switch` over an enum's `->value` at the call site — logic that belongs on the enum but lives elsewhere instead.

sin_in-array-mirrors-enum.title: InArrayMirrorsEnum
sin_in-array-mirrors-enum.help: `in_array($x, [literals])` whose literals mirror an existing enum's cases

sin_match-default-returns-null.title: MatchDefaultReturnsNull
sin_match-default-returns-null.help: `match` `default` that returns `null`/`false`/`[]` (or has no body) instead of throwing

sin_string-match-mirrors-enum.title: StringMatchMirrorsEnum
sin_string-match-mirrors-enum.help: `match`/`switch` over string/int literals that mirror an existing backed enum's case values

sin_unnamed-vocabulary-literal.title: UnnamedVocabularyLiteral
sin_unnamed-vocabulary-literal.help: A raw string in an argument the codebase elsewhere fills from a named vocabulary — `expect('{')` beside `expect(Token::COLON)`, where `Token::BRACE_OPEN` already names it

sin_generic-exception.title: GenericException
sin_generic-exception.help: `throw new <bare SPL>` (RuntimeException/LogicException/…) instead of a named type

sin_message-at-throw.title: MessageAtThrow
sin_message-at-throw.help: Message string built at the throw site (no domain values / named factory)

sin_swallow-catch.title: SwallowCatch
sin_swallow-catch.help: `catch` whose only effect is `return null/false/[]`; empty catch (silent swallow)

sin_wrapping-without-cause.title: WrappingWithoutCause
sin_wrapping-without-cause.help: Wrapping a caught exception without passing it as `previous`/cause

sin_constructor-side-effect.title: ConstructorSideEffect
sin_constructor-side-effect.help: A constructor that performs a side effect on a collaborator and throws away the result, so simply creating the object changes something outside it.

sin_divergent-twin.title: DivergentTwin
sin_divergent-twin.help: Two functions do the same job, but one of them skips a step the other takes — usually a fix made in one copy and forgotten in the other.

sin_duplicate-function.title: DuplicateFunction
sin_duplicate-function.help: Copy-pasted code — two+ functions with an identical AST (formatting/comments aside)

sin_manufactured-fake-fill.title: ManufacturedFakeFill
sin_manufactured-fake-fill.help: `?? <empty literal>` filling a required slot (manufactured fake)

sin_mutable-static-state.title: MutableStaticState
sin_mutable-static-state.help: A write to a static property — really a global variable with a namespace attached — where whichever write happens last wins, so the order code runs in changes the result.

sin_near-duplicate-function.title: NearDuplicateFunction
sin_near-duplicate-function.help: Redundant methods — two+ functions with the same SHAPE differing only in names/literals (type-2 clone)

sin_coalesced-loop-subject.title: CoalescedLoopSubject
sin_coalesced-loop-subject.help: `foreach ($x[$k] ?? [] as …)` — the absence check buried in the loop header instead of stated as a guard

sin_if-else-ladder.title: IfElseLadder
sin_if-else-ladder.help: if/elseif ladder of 4+ branches (should be match/dispatch)

sin_inline-throw.title: InlineThrow
sin_inline-throw.help: `?? throw` fed into a call or dereferenced on the same line (inline throw mid-expression)

sin_loop-inverted-guard.title: LoopInvertedGuard
sin_loop-inverted-guard.help: Loop body (multi-statement) wrapped in an `if` instead of `continue` guard

sin_non-counting-for.title: NonCountingFor
sin_non-counting-for.help: A `for` loop that looks like it's counting, but its step actually assigns the next item instead of incrementing a counter.

sin_redundant-else.title: RedundantElse
sin_redundant-else.help: `else` after an `if` branch that already returns/throws (redundant)

sin_short-circuit-statement.title: ShortCircuitStatement
sin_short-circuit-statement.help: a bare `$a && $b->do();` statement — a short-circuit whose result nothing reads, so the operator is an `if` in disguise

sin_ternary-statement.title: TernaryStatement
sin_ternary-statement.help: a bare `$cond ? doThis() : doThat();` statement — a ternary whose value nothing reads, so it is choosing an ACTION, not a value

sin_dead-config-key.title: DeadConfigKey
sin_dead-config-key.help: A config key nothing reads — dead surface left behind by a deleted feature, which new code may wrongly adopt

sin_dead-event-wiring.title: DeadEventWiring
sin_dead-event-wiring.help: An `Event::listen` on an event class no live code path can fire — a listener chain that dead-ends but reads as live wiring

sin_duplicated-config-default.title: DuplicatedConfigDefault
sin_duplicated-config-default.help: A config key whose default is stated TWICE — once in the config file, again as the reader's inline fallback — two sources of truth that drift silently

sin_mass-update-at-call-site.title: MassUpdateAtCallSite
sin_mass-update-at-call-site.help: Bare `$model->update([...])` mass-array update at a call site

sin_model-mutation-at-call-site.title: ModelMutationAtCallSite
sin_model-mutation-at-call-site.help: Set-property-then-`save()` at a call site (should be an intention method)

sin_orphaned-binding.title: OrphanedBinding
sin_orphaned-binding.help: A container binding whose abstract nothing ever resolves — dead wiring that reads as load-bearing and survives every refactor

sin_request-accessor-recast.title: RequestAccessorRecast
sin_request-accessor-recast.help: Re-coercing a typed request accessor at a call site — `$request->string('id')->toString()` or `(string) $request->string('id')` instead of a named getter on a request class

sin_bare-state-predicate.title: BareStatePredicate
sin_bare-state-predicate.help: A `bool` about the object's own state named as a bare verb — `binds()`, `spins()` — where a question belongs

sin_narrated-command.title: NarratedCommand
sin_narrated-command.help: A command named in the third person — `hides()`, `entersTestMode()` — where a call is an order, not a description of one

sin_constructor-orchestration.title: ConstructorOrchestration
sin_constructor-orchestration.help: A page object fills a public slot imperatively in the constructor (`$this->x = $this->projector->…()`) where a `#[Computed]` property hook would describe it in place

sin_injected-service-not-hidden.title: InjectedServiceNotHidden
sin_injected-service-not-hidden.help: A page object injects a service (`#[FromContainer]`, …) into a public property without `#[Hidden]` — it leaks into the generated TypeScript type

sin_manual-output-transform.title: ManualOutputTransform
sin_manual-output-transform.help: A `Data` computed slot hand-flattens a value object into a wire array, instead of a `#[WithTransformer]` that owns the serialized shape

sin_page-object-missing-typescript.title: PageObjectMissingTypeScript
sin_page-object-missing-typescript.help: A page object travels back in a response but carries no `#[TypeScript]` — the `.vue` page reads it as untyped `any`, so the whole page-prop contract goes unchecked

sin_service-location-in-page-object.title: ServiceLocationInPageObject
sin_service-location-in-page-object.help: A page object reaches into the container with `app()`/`resolve()` instead of injecting the collaborator via `#[FromContainer]`

sin_transformer-without-ts-type.title: TransformerWithoutTsType
sin_transformer-without-ts-type.help: A `#[WithTransformer]` changes a property's wire shape but has no paired `#[TypeScriptType]`/`#[LiteralTypeScriptType]`, so the generated TypeScript keeps the wrong (PHP) type

sin_computed-boolean-argument.title: ComputedBooleanArgument
sin_computed-boolean-argument.help: A parameter that's just true/false, computed by every caller from the same object it could be given instead.

sin_converted-argument.title: ConvertedArgument
sin_converted-argument.help: A parameter typed as the already-converted form instead of the raw value, so every call site repeats the same conversion before calling it (e.g. `Raises::of(ClassAlias::of($interaction), …)`).

sin_derived-argument.title: DerivedArgument
sin_derived-argument.help: Passing the same object twice — once whole and once broken into a piece (`persist($request, $request->shopId())`), or broken into several pieces at once (`new AgentTurn($r->output(), $r->failed(), $r->errorOutput())`) — when the callee could derive each piece itself from the one object.

sin_param-resolved-from-param.title: ParamResolvedFromParam
sin_param-resolved-from-param.help: Unpacking the target out of a container parameter — a method takes `(Workflow $workflow, string $nodeId)` and resolves `$workflow->graph->nodeById($nodeId)` itself, when it could just receive the node directly.

sin_repeated-guard.title: RepeatedGuard
sin_repeated-guard.help: The SAME compound guard condition recurs in ≥2 places — the same check spelled differently (inline reaches vs locals) or reordered still counts, so a copied condition has no name

sin_repeated-named-call.title: RepeatedNamedCall
sin_repeated-named-call.help: The same `with`-style (variadic) method is called with the same named argument at 2+ sites, instead of a named helper on the type

sin_repeated-type-guard.title: RepeatedTypeGuard
sin_repeated-type-guard.help: The SAME multi-`instanceof` type-narrowing guard (`$x instanceof A && $x->y instanceof B`) is written verbatim in ≥2 places — a check with no name, copied instead of named

sin_nullable-registry-lookup.title: NullableRegistryLookup
sin_nullable-registry-lookup.help: A keyed-store `get()` that returns `null` on a miss (should resolve-or-throw)

sin_boundary-duplicated-operation.title: BoundaryDuplicatedOperation
sin_boundary-duplicated-operation.help: The same domain operation hand-rolled at two DIFFERENT entry boundaries (a console command and an MCP tool, a controller and a command) — one operation with two implementations that drift

sin_dangling-route-name.title: DanglingRouteName
sin_dangling-route-name.help: A `route('x')` lookup naming a route no registration mints — a stringly cross-reference that only fails at runtime, as a 500

sin_duplicate-route.title: DuplicateRoute
sin_duplicate-route.help: Two route registrations of the same verb bind different URLs to the SAME `[Controller, method]` — two names for one handler (invokable single-action controllers, commonly aliased to several canonical URLs, are exempt)

sin_duplicate-route-action.title: DuplicateRouteAction
sin_duplicate-route-action.help: Two route actions in different controllers thinly delegate to the SAME operation (`return $this->exporter->export(...)`) — the same entry point twice

sin_route-delegates-to-controller.title: RouteDelegatesToController
sin_route-delegates-to-controller.help: A route action forwards to ANOTHER controller's action (`return $this->otherController->action(...)`) — a redundant entry point onto an operation that already has one

sin_all-nullable-data.title: AllNullableData
sin_all-nullable-data.help: All-nullable "god" DTO — every field `?T`/defaulted (type doesn't tell the truth)

sin_all-optional-data.title: AllOptionalData
sin_all-optional-data.help: Every field of a `Data` object is `T|Optional` — the type promises nothing is ever present; the absence belongs on the CONTAINER field where it's used

sin_data-collection-type.title: DataCollectionType
sin_data-collection-type.help: A `Data` property is TYPED as `DataCollection` — it should be `array` (or `Collection`) with `#[DataCollectionOf(X)]`; the `DataCollection` type emits malformed TypeScript and skips element-typed hydration

sin_data-method-hint-collision.title: DataMethodHintCollision
sin_data-method-hint-collision.help: `@method` tag that re-declares a real method (names the concrete factory, not the magic `from`/`collect`)

sin_hook-missing-computed.title: HookMissingComputed
sin_hook-missing-computed.help: A get-only property HOOK on a `Data` class lacks `#[Computed]` — Spatie reads the virtual property as a hydration INPUT, expects it in `::from()`, and crashes or silently drops it

sin_manual-hydration-loop.title: ManualHydrationLoop
sin_manual-hydration-loop.help: Collections hydrated with `::from()` per item instead of `#[DataCollectionOf]` + `::collect()`

sin_manual-input-cast.title: ManualInputCast
sin_manual-input-cast.help: A `Data` value-object property is hand-built at every construction site, instead of a `#[WithCast]` / `Castable` that owns the hydration once

sin_nested-type-missing-typescript.title: NestedTypeMissingTypeScript
sin_nested-type-missing-typescript.help: A `#[TypeScript]` Data has a property typed as a nested `Data` class that itself lacks `#[TypeScript]` — the transformer emits it as `undefined`, a silent hole in the generated type (a nested enum is fine; the enum collector auto-generates it)

sin_non-final-data.title: NonFinalData
sin_non-final-data.help: Data class not `final` / props not `readonly` promoted

sin_null-to-optional-map.title: NullToOptionalMap
sin_null-to-optional-map.help: A producer hand-maps null→`new Optional` — `$x === null ? new Optional : Foo::from($x)` or `expr() ?? new Optional` — instead of one named factory (Spatie's `optional()` maps null→null, the opposite of what a `T|Optional` slot needs)

sin_nullable-wire-object.title: NullableWireObject
sin_nullable-wire-object.help: A nested object on a `#[TypeScript]` Data is typed `T | null` — it ships `null` on the wire where `T | Optional` would OMIT it (what the frontend's `x?.` reads for "absent")

sin_prefer-optional-create.title: PreferOptionalCreate
sin_prefer-optional-create.help: A raw `new Optional` is constructed in a runtime expression where Spatie's built-in `Optional::create()` factory reads clearer

sin_data-to-array-roundtrip.title: DataToArrayRoundtrip
sin_data-to-array-roundtrip.help: A `X::from(...)->toArray()` sits in a `::from` slot typed `X` that re-hydrates it — build → array → build

sin_derived-collection-cast.title: DerivedCollectionCast
sin_derived-collection-cast.help: A `#[DataCollectionOf]` is filled by mapping a factory over inputs at the call site, where a `#[WithCast]` should own the derivation

sin_hand-key-remap.title: HandKeyRemap
sin_hand-key-remap.help: A `::from([...])` mechanically renames `$src['snake_key']` → `camelKey` by hand, instead of a class-level `#[MapInputName]`

sin_redundant-enum-unwrap.title: RedundantEnumUnwrap
sin_redundant-enum-unwrap.help: An enum is unwrapped to `->value` at a hydration site (`'status' => $order->status->value`) where the property is typed as that enum — Spatie re-casts the scalar straight back to the enum

sin_redundant-native-cast.title: RedundantNativeCast
sin_redundant-native-cast.help: An enum / date is constructed at a hydration site (`Enum::from($x)`, `new DateTime($x)`) where the property auto-casts the raw scalar

sin_redundant-nested-from.title: RedundantNestedFrom
sin_redundant-nested-from.help: A nested `X::from([...])` fills a slot the parent `::from` already auto-hydrates from the array

sin_feature-envy.title: FeatureEnvy
sin_feature-envy.help: Exiled behaviour / feature envy — a method operating on ONE other owned object's internals that belongs ON that object

sin_keyed-lookup-envy.title: KeyedLookupEnvy
sin_keyed-lookup-envy.help: Indirect feature envy — a method that uses an owned object's IDENTITY as a key to look up a fact about it through a collaborator

sin_type-switch.title: TypeSwitch
sin_type-switch.help: two or more `instanceof` tests on the same subject deciding different branches — asking a value what it IS instead of telling it what to do

sin_assembled-template.title: AssembledTemplate
sin_assembled-template.help: A multi-line template assembled as an array of line fragments and joined with a newline — the output is unreadable in the source that emits it

sin_masked-invariant.title: MaskedInvariant
sin_masked-invariant.help: Masked invariant — an own field read as `?->… ?? <fake literal>`, even though the very operation sets that field first, so the fallback only ever answers an impossible "not set yet".

sin_phantom-nullable.title: PhantomNullable
sin_phantom-nullable.help: Phantom nullable — a field typed `?T` (promoted param or declared property, any class) whose value, traced through the whole program, is always read as present and NEVER guarded, so the null never happens

sin_placeholder-filled-data.title: PlaceholderFilledData
sin_placeholder-filled-data.help: A required non-nullable `string` slot handed `''` — the type promises a value that is always there and the caller has none

sin_redundant-arrow-return-type.title: RedundantArrowReturnType
sin_redundant-arrow-return-type.help: An arrow function whose return type only repeats what its one expression provably yields — `fn (): string => $this->name` on a `string` property

sin_scratch-state-restore.title: ScratchStateRestore
sin_scratch-state-restore.help: Scratch state on `$this` — a method that saves one of its own fields to a local and restores it (`$prev = $this->scope; … $this->scope = $prev`), the field really a per-call input

sin_useless-property-hook.title: UselessPropertyHook
sin_useless-property-hook.help: A `get` hook that reads nothing from `$this` — a stored property wearing computed syntax

sin_array-bag.title: ArrayBag
sin_array-bag.help: String-indexing (`$arr['key']`) a structured array param instead of giving it a name — the type was never defined.

sin_array-return-bag.title: ArrayReturnBag
sin_array-return-bag.help: Returning a multi-field string-keyed array literal (a bag that should be a value object)

sin_coupled-fields.title: CoupledFields
sin_coupled-fields.help: A class's own fields always change and get checked together — one concept split across several fields — and should be folded into a single value object.

sin_data-clump.title: DataClump
sin_data-clump.help: The same 3+ scalar params threaded through 2+ classes (a recurring data clump → one object)

sin_flat-field-cluster.title: FlatFieldCluster
sin_flat-field-cluster.help: A `#[TypeScript]` `Data` class spreads a value object it already models flat across sibling scalar fields sharing a camelCase prefix (`wireType` + `wireLabel`) instead of nesting the existing `Wire{type, label}`.

sin_hand-rolled-wither.title: HandRolledWither
sin_hand-rolled-wither.help: A wither method rebuilds the whole object by re-listing every constructor field, so adding a new field means updating every wither in the class.

sin_mutable-value-object.title: MutableValueObject
sin_mutable-value-object.help: A value type that mutates its own field after construction, so two things holding what should be the same value can end up different — one changes without the other knowing.

sin_positional-tuple-return.title: PositionalTupleReturn
sin_positional-tuple-return.help: Returning a positional TUPLE — `return [$node, $key, $inputs, $outputs]` — bundling independent values as a keyless list the caller destructures by position

sin_raw-decoded-array-return.title: RawDecodedArrayReturn
sin_raw-decoded-array-return.help: Returning a raw decoded boundary array (`json_decode(...)`) untyped

sin_csharp-blank-string-default.title: BlankStringDefault
sin_csharp-blank-string-default.help: a `string` parameter or property defaulted to `""` and then checked with `== ""` or `string.IsNullOrEmpty` — the blank is being used to mean "missing"

sin_csharp-cancelled-coalesce.title: CancelledCoalesce
sin_csharp-cancelled-coalesce.help: a `??` fallback compared against the same value it falls back to — `(name ?? "") != ""` — so "missing" and "empty" end up in one branch without saying so

sin_csharp-de-nulled-finder.title: DeNulledFinder
sin_csharp-de-nulled-finder.help: a finder returning a nullable object whose every caller asserts it is there — `Find(id)!`, `Find(id) ?? throw …` — a miss the finder should have refused itself

sin_csharp-invented-default.title: InventedDefault
sin_csharp-invented-default.help: `F(x ?? "")` — an empty string, `0` or `false` invented to fill an argument, or answered by a lookup helper on a miss, a stand-in the callee cannot tell from real data

sin_csharp-null-forgiven.title: NullForgiven
sin_csharp-null-forgiven.help: The null-forgiving `!` on a value declared nullable — the compiler told the caller it may be null, and `!` silences it instead of deciding

sin_csharp-flag-argument.title: FlagArgument
sin_csharp-flag-argument.help: a method whose whole body branches on a `bool` parameter — `if (compact) … else …` — two methods sharing one name

sin_csharp-member-after-method.title: MemberAfterMethod
sin_csharp-member-after-method.help: a field, constant or stored property declared below a constructor or a method — the type's state hidden among its behaviour

sin_csharp-member-out-of-order.title: MemberOutOfOrder
sin_csharp-member-out-of-order.help: a `const` or `static readonly` value declared below a field or a stored property — the top of the type read in no particular order

sin_csharp-namespace-cycle.title: NamespaceCycle
sin_csharp-namespace-cycle.help: two of the project's namespaces that each use the other — a cycle that makes them one namespace split under two names

sin_csharp-namespace-dependency.title: NamespaceDependency
sin_csharp-namespace-dependency.help: a reference out of a declared layer into a namespace that layer did not declare it may use

sin_csharp-archaeology-comment.title: ArchaeologyComment
sin_csharp-archaeology-comment.help: a comment that tells the code's past — `// formerly lived in CheckoutService`, `// refactored to use the cache` — describing a version nobody is reading

sin_csharp-bloated-docblock.title: BloatedDocblock
sin_csharp-bloated-docblock.help: a type whose doc comment runs to two or more paragraphs — usually a sign the type does too much

sin_csharp-ceremony-docblock.title: CeremonyDocblock
sin_csharp-ceremony-docblock.help: a doc comment whose every tag is empty or only repeats the signature — `<param name="order">The order.</param>`, an empty `<returns>`

sin_csharp-dangling-doc-reference.title: DanglingDocReference
sin_csharp-dangling-doc-reference.help: a `<see cref>` that resolves to nothing from where it is written — a name the project no longer declares, or one spelled so it does not reach it

sin_csharp-negative-space-comment.title: NegativeSpaceComment
sin_csharp-negative-space-comment.help: a comment defending the code against a reading nobody made — `// not magic, just a day`, `// deliberately not sorted` — saying what it is not instead of what it is

sin_csharp-restated-comment.title: RestatedComment
sin_csharp-restated-comment.help: a comment above a statement whose every word the statement already spells — `// set the total to the order total` over `var total = order.Total;`

sin_duplicate-csharp-method.title: DuplicateMethod
sin_duplicate-csharp-method.help: Copy-pasted code — two+ C# methods, accessors or local functions with an identical body, formatting, comments and attributes aside

sin_near-duplicate-csharp-method.title: NearDuplicateMethod
sin_near-duplicate-csharp-method.help: A near-copy — two+ C# methods, accessors or local functions with one control-flow skeleton that differ only in their local names or the literals they use (a key, a route, a message)

sin_csharp-const-class-enum.title: ConstClassEnum
sin_csharp-const-class-enum.help: a class that holds nothing but `const` strings or numbers — a closed set of values written as constants instead of an `enum`

sin_csharp-enum-case-or-chain.title: EnumCaseOrChain
sin_csharp-enum-case-or-chain.help: `s == Status.Paid || s == Status.Refunded` (or `s is Status.Paid or Status.Refunded`) — a group of enum cases tested by hand at the call site

sin_csharp-in-array-mirrors-enum.title: InArrayMirrorsEnum
sin_csharp-in-array-mirrors-enum.help: `new[] { "paid", "refunded" }.Contains(status)` or `status is "paid" or "refunded"` — a list of strings that repeats the members of an enum the code already has

sin_csharp-match-default-returns-null.title: MatchDefaultReturnsNull
sin_csharp-match-default-returns-null.help: a `switch` that names every member of an enum, then answers `null`, `default` or `false` in its `_` arm — the one value that arm can see is a bug, and it is answered as if it were fine

sin_csharp-string-mirrors-enum.title: StringMirrorsEnum
sin_csharp-string-mirrors-enum.help: A `switch` or an `if` ladder dispatching on strings that are the names of an enum the codebase already declares — the enum, written out again as text

sin_csharp-unnamed-vocabulary-literal.title: UnnamedVocabularyLiteral
sin_csharp-unnamed-vocabulary-literal.help: a raw string handed to a parameter the codebase elsewhere fills from a named constant — `Expect("{")` beside `Expect(Token.Colon)`, where `Token.BraceOpen` already names it

sin_csharp-generic-throw.title: GenericThrow
sin_csharp-generic-throw.help: `throw new Exception/InvalidOperationException("…")` — a failure that names nothing, described in prose at the throw site

sin_csharp-swallowed-exception.title: SwallowedException
sin_csharp-swallowed-exception.help: A bare `catch` or `catch (Exception)` whose body is empty, continues, or returns nothing — every failure, expected or not, made to vanish

sin_csharp-wrapping-without-cause.title: WrappingWithoutCause
sin_csharp-wrapping-without-cause.help: a `catch` that throws a new exception without passing the caught one as its inner exception, so the original stack trace is lost

sin_csharp-constructor-side-effect.title: ConstructorSideEffect
sin_csharp-constructor-side-effect.help: a constructor that calls a method on something it was handed and ignores the result — just creating the object changes something outside it

sin_csharp-mutable-static-state.title: MutableStaticState
sin_csharp-mutable-static-state.help: a `static` field that methods write to — state no instance owns, changed by whichever code ran last

sin_csharp-coalesced-loop-subject.title: CoalescedLoopSubject
sin_csharp-coalesced-loop-subject.help: a `foreach` over `items ?? []` (or `Enumerable.Empty<T>()`, or a new empty list) — the check for a missing collection is hidden in the loop header

sin_csharp-inline-throw.title: InlineThrow
sin_csharp-inline-throw.help: a `?? throw` inside a call's argument or in front of a member call — the check that stops the method is hidden in the middle of the work

sin_csharp-loop-wrapped-in-if.title: LoopWrappedInIf
sin_csharp-loop-wrapped-in-if.help: A `for`, `foreach` or `while` whose whole body is one `if` (no `else`) around real work — the iteration pushed a level deep behind a condition

sin_csharp-nested-ternary.title: NestedTernary
sin_csharp-nested-ternary.help: a `?:` with another `?:` as one of its branches — several decisions packed into one expression

sin_csharp-non-counting-for.title: NonCountingFor
sin_csharp-non-counting-for.help: a `for` loop whose step assigns the next item instead of moving a counter — a walk written as a count

sin_csharp-subject-ladder.title: SubjectLadder
sin_csharp-subject-ladder.help: An `if`/`else if` chain of four or more rungs that each compare the same subject with a constant — a dispatch written as a ladder.

sin_deep-csharp-nesting.title: DeepNesting
sin_deep-csharp-nesting.help: An `if`, loop or `switch` opening a fourth level of choices inside one C# method — an arrow of conditions and loops

sin_redundant-csharp-else.title: RedundantElse
sin_redundant-csharp-else.help: An `else` after an `if` branch that already left — it ends in `return`, `throw`, `continue` or `break` — indenting the rest of the method for nothing

sin_csharp-bare-state-predicate.title: BareStatePredicate
sin_csharp-bare-state-predicate.help: a `bool` about the object's own state named as a claim — `Binds()`, `Spins` — where a question belongs

sin_csharp-converted-argument.title: ConvertedArgument
sin_csharp-converted-argument.help: a scalar parameter its callers keep filling with the same conversion — `ReceiptFor(order.Id.ToString())` call after call — because it asks for the converted form instead of the value

sin_csharp-derived-argument.title: DerivedArgument
sin_csharp-derived-argument.help: a call that hands over an object and a projection of it — `Persist(request, request.ChannelId)` — or an object in three pieces, where the method could read them itself

sin_csharp-param-resolved-from-param.title: ParamResolvedFromParam
sin_csharp-param-resolved-from-param.help: a method that takes a container and a key and first resolves one against the other — `Rename(Workflow workflow, string nodeId)` doing `workflow.Graph.Node(nodeId)` — when it only wanted what the key names

sin_csharp-repeated-guard.title: RepeatedGuard
sin_csharp-repeated-guard.help: the same compound condition — `order.Paid && !order.Cancelled` — written at two or more sites, a question with no name

sin_csharp-repeated-named-call.title: RepeatedNamedCall
sin_csharp-repeated-named-call.help: the same `with` copy — `order with { Status = OrderStatus.Shipped }` — written at two or more sites, an operation the record never named

sin_csharp-repeated-type-guard.title: RepeatedTypeGuard
sin_csharp-repeated-type-guard.help: the same chain of type checks — `node is Invocation call && call.Target is MemberAccess` — written at two or more sites, a shape with no name

sin_csharp-feature-envy.title: FeatureEnvy
sin_csharp-feature-envy.help: a method that loops another object's collection or writes its members, reaching into it more than into its own state — behaviour exiled from the object it works on

sin_csharp-type-switch.title: TypeSwitch
sin_csharp-type-switch.help: `shape switch { Circle c => …, Square s => … }` — asking which of your own types a value is, to decide what to do with it

sin_csharp-assembled-template.title: AssembledTemplate
sin_csharp-assembled-template.help: `string.Join("\n", new[] { "public class X", "{", "}" })` or `sb.AppendLine("…")` line after line — a multi-line text built from line fragments, so its shape cannot be seen in the source

sin_csharp-placeholder-filled-data.title: PlaceholderFilledData
sin_csharp-placeholder-filled-data.help: `new Card(title, "")` — a record's required `string` filled with a blank so the record can be built, hiding a missing value no type check can see

sin_csharp-array-return-bag.title: ArrayReturnBag
sin_csharp-array-return-bag.help: a method that returns `new Dictionary<string, object> { ["sku"] = …, ["qty"] = … }` — a record with fixed fields, handed back as a dictionary

sin_csharp-coupled-fields.title: CoupledFields
sin_csharp-coupled-fields.help: a type whose own fields always travel together — assembled into one value again and again, null-checked together, or one copying what a sibling field already holds — one concept held as several fields

sin_csharp-data-clump.title: DataClump
sin_csharp-data-clump.help: The same three or more string, number, date or id parameters threaded through methods of two or more types — values that always travel together but have no type of their own.

sin_csharp-dictionary-bag.title: DictionaryBag
sin_csharp-dictionary-bag.help: A string-keyed dictionary or JSON object read by keys written in the source — `row["sku"]`, `json.GetProperty("name")` — a record nobody declared

sin_csharp-mutable-value-object.title: MutableValueObject
sin_csharp-mutable-value-object.help: a record that can change after it is built — a `set` accessor, or a method that writes its own state — so two holders of the same value can end up seeing different things

sin_csharp-positional-tuple-return.title: PositionalTupleReturn
sin_csharp-positional-tuple-return.help: a method that returns `(decimal, decimal, string)` — unnamed values the caller reads by position, where two of the same type can be swapped and nothing notices

sin_mirrored-server-type.title: MirroredServerType
sin_mirrored-server-type.help: A hand-written TypeScript type mirrors a backend `Data` class one-to-one — two sources of truth for one contract that drift the moment the server shape changes

sin_compound-inline-component.title: CompoundInlineComponent
sin_compound-inline-component.help: A compound primitive (`Dialog`/`Card`/`Sheet`/`Tabs`…) assembled inline with a substantial body — extract it into its own named component.

sin_deep-data-reach.title: DeepDataReach
sin_deep-data-reach.help: A group of elements in a sizeable template that all reach deep into the same nested object (≥2 distinct fields) — extract the shared mid-object into a component that takes it as a prop.

sin_deep-nested.title: DeepNested
sin_deep-nested.help: Template markup nested far too deep — extract a subtree as its own component

sin_duplicate-element.title: DuplicateElement
sin_duplicate-element.help: Identical markup (3+ elements) repeated 2+ times — within a template or across components — extract one component

sin_near-duplicate-element.title: NearDuplicateElement
sin_near-duplicate-element.help: Markup with one skeleton repeated 2+ times — the same tags, attributes and nesting binding different data — within a template, across components, or as two components' whole templates

sin_prop-drilling.title: PropDrilling
sin_prop-drilling.help: A prop forwarded through a chain of 2+ components, none of which read it — passed down through components that only pass it further.

sin_prop-mutation.title: PropMutation
sin_prop-mutation.help: A prop is written to — `v-model` bound to it, or `@event="prop = …"` — but props are read-only (a build error or a silent no-op).

sin_control-flow-on-element.title: ControlFlowOnElement
sin_control-flow-on-element.help: `v-if`/`v-for`/`v-else`/`v-else-if` on an HTML/component tag instead of a `<template>`

sin_index-as-key.title: IndexAsKey
sin_index-as-key.help: `:key` bound to the `v-for` index — a positional key corrupts state when the list reorders or an item is inserted

sin_loop-with-condition.title: LoopWithCondition
sin_loop-with-condition.help: `v-for` and `v-if`/`v-else-if` on the same element — the condition is re-evaluated every iteration.

sin_switch-case.title: SwitchCase
sin_switch-case.help: A `v-if`/`v-else-if` chain re-testing the same subject (should be `<SwitchCase :value>`)

sin_python-blank-string-default.title: BlankStringDefault
sin_python-blank-string-default.help: `x: str = ""` standing in for absence — then asked `x == ""`, `not x` or `if x:` in its own scope

sin_python-cancelled-fallback.title: CancelledFallback
sin_python-cancelled-fallback.help: `(x or "") != ""` — a value defaulted to a blank only to be compared against that same blank, so a missing value and an empty one are treated the same without saying so.

sin_python-conditional-spread.title: ConditionalSpread
sin_python-conditional-spread.help: `**({"k": v} if v else {})` / `*([x] if x else [])` — an entry is spread in only when present, using a conditional that turns absence into an empty collection.

sin_python-invented-default.title: InventedDefault
sin_python-invented-default.help: `f(x or "")` — an empty string, `0` or `False` invented to fill an argument when the value is missing, a stand-in the callee cannot tell from real data

sin_python-nullable-callback.title: NullableCallback
sin_python-nullable-callback.help: `cb: Callable | None = None` asked `if cb is not None:` / `if cb:` / `cb or …` in the body — a no-op treated as if it might be missing.

sin_python-flag-argument.title: FlagArgument
sin_python-flag-argument.help: a function whose whole body branches on a `bool` parameter — or on whether an optional one was given — two functions sharing one name

sin_python-member-after-method.title: MemberAfterMethod
sin_python-member-after-method.help: a constant, class attribute or field declared below a method — the class's state hidden among its behaviour

sin_python-member-out-of-order.title: MemberOutOfOrder
sin_python-member-out-of-order.help: a constant declared below a field in the head of a class — the inventory read in an ad-hoc order

sin_python-namespace-cycle.title: NamespaceCycle
sin_python-namespace-cycle.help: two of the project's packages import each other — a cycle that makes them one package split under two names.

sin_python-namespace-dependency.title: NamespaceDependency
sin_python-namespace-dependency.help: an import out of a declared layer into a package that layer did not declare it may use

sin_python-archaeology-comment.title: ArchaeologyComment
sin_python-archaeology-comment.help: a comment or docstring narrating the code's history — where it lived, what it replaced, what it no longer is

sin_python-bloated-docblock.title: BloatedDocblock
sin_python-bloated-docblock.help: a class docstring of two or more paragraphs of prose — an essay that says the class does too much

sin_python-ceremony-docblock.title: CeremonyDocblock
sin_python-ceremony-docblock.help: a docstring with no summary whose every entry restates the annotated signature — `order (Order):`, `:rtype: int`

sin_python-dangling-doc-reference.title: DanglingDocReference
sin_python-dangling-doc-reference.help: a Sphinx cross-reference in a docstring (`:class:`shop.cart.Basket``) to a first-party name the codebase no longer declares

sin_python-negative-space-comment.title: NegativeSpaceComment
sin_python-negative-space-comment.help: a comment or docstring defending the code against a misunderstanding nobody actually had — what it is not, rather than what it is.

sin_python-restated-comment.title: RestatedComment
sin_python-restated-comment.help: a `#` comment that only narrates the statement below it — every word of it already spelled by the code

sin_duplicate-python-function.title: DuplicateFunction
sin_duplicate-python-function.help: Copy-pasted code — two+ Python functions or methods with an identical body, formatting, comments and docstrings aside

sin_near-duplicate-python-function.title: NearDuplicateFunction
sin_near-duplicate-python-function.help: A near-copy — two+ Python functions or methods with one control-flow skeleton that differ only in their local names or the literals they use (a path, a key, a message)

sin_python-constant-class-enum.title: ConstantClassEnum
sin_python-constant-class-enum.help: a class that is nothing but `PENDING = "pending"` constants — a closed set of values written out by hand instead of an `Enum`

sin_python-enum-case-or-chain.title: EnumCaseOrChain
sin_python-enum-case-or-chain.help: `s == Status.PENDING or s == Status.LATE` — a group of an enum's members re-derived at the call site instead of named on the enum

sin_python-enum-value-match.title: EnumValueMatch
sin_python-enum-value-match.help: `match status.value: case "paid": …` at a call site — the enum's raw values matched again where the enum could answer

sin_python-in-literals-mirrors-enum.title: InLiteralsMirrorsEnum
sin_python-in-literals-mirrors-enum.help: `x in ("pending", "late")` whose literals are an existing enum's values — a group of its members spelled as raw strings at the call site

sin_python-match-wildcard-returns-none.title: MatchWildcardReturnsNone
sin_python-match-wildcard-returns-none.help: a `match` over an enum's members whose `case _:` returns `None` — a member nobody handled answers nothing instead of failing

sin_python-string-match-mirrors-enum.title: StringMatchMirrorsEnum
sin_python-string-match-mirrors-enum.help: `match raw: case "pending": …` whose cases are an existing enum's values — dispatching on loose strings the enum already seals

sin_python-unnamed-vocabulary-literal.title: UnnamedVocabularyLiteral
sin_python-unnamed-vocabulary-literal.help: a raw string handed to a parameter the codebase elsewhere fills from a named constant — `expect("{")` beside `expect(Token.COLON)`, where `Token.BRACE_OPEN` already names it

sin_python-message-string-raise.title: MessageStringRaise
sin_python-message-string-raise.help: `raise Exception/RuntimeError("…")` — a failure that names nothing, described in prose at the raise site

sin_python-raise-without-cause.title: RaiseWithoutCause
sin_python-raise-without-cause.help: `raise Other(...)` inside an `except` block with no `from` — the failure being handled left as an implicit context, never named as the cause

sin_python-swallowed-exception.title: SwallowedException
sin_python-swallowed-exception.help: A bare `except:` or `except Exception` whose body only passes, continues or returns nothing — every failure, expected or not, made to vanish

sin_python-constructor-side-effect.title: ConstructorSideEffect
sin_python-constructor-side-effect.help: an `__init__` that tells a collaborator to act and throws the answer away — merely building the object has an effect outside it.

sin_python-divergent-twin.title: DivergentTwin
sin_python-divergent-twin.help: two functions do the same job, but one of them skips a step the other takes — usually a fix made in one copy and forgotten in the other.

sin_python-mutable-static-state.title: MutableStaticState
sin_python-mutable-static-state.help: a `global` written from a function, or a class attribute set from a method — state no instance owns, changed by whoever ran last

sin_deep-python-nesting.title: DeepNesting
sin_deep-python-nesting.help: An `if`, loop or `match` opening a fourth level of choices inside one Python function — an arrow of conditions and loops

sin_python-coalesced-loop-subject.title: CoalescedLoopSubject
sin_python-coalesced-loop-subject.help: `for x in d.get(k, [])` / `for x in y or []` over a parameter — whether the caller handed anything over, decided in the loop header instead of stated as a guard

sin_python-conditional-statement.title: ConditionalStatement
sin_python-conditional-statement.help: a bare `a() if x else b()` statement — a conditional expression whose value nothing reads, so it chooses an action, not a value.

sin_python-loop-wrapped-in-if.title: LoopWrappedInIf
sin_python-loop-wrapped-in-if.help: A `for` or `while` whose whole body is one `if` (no `else`) around real work — the iteration pushed a level deep behind a condition

sin_python-nested-conditional.title: NestedConditional
sin_python-nested-conditional.help: `a if x else b if y else c` — a conditional expression inside another's branch, a branching decision folded into one line

sin_python-short-circuit-statement.title: ShortCircuitStatement
sin_python-short-circuit-statement.help: a bare `a and b()` or `a or b()` statement — an `and`/`or` whose value nothing reads, so the operator is really acting as an `if`.

sin_python-subject-ladder.title: SubjectLadder
sin_python-subject-ladder.help: An `if`/`elif` chain of four or more rungs that each test the same subject for equality with a constant — a dispatch written as a ladder.

sin_redundant-python-else.title: RedundantElse
sin_redundant-python-else.help: An `else:` after an `if` branch that already left — it ends in `return`, `raise`, `continue` or `break` — indenting the rest of the function for nothing

sin_python-bare-state-predicate.title: BareStatePredicate
sin_python-bare-state-predicate.help: a `bool` about the object's own state named as a bare verb — `binds()`, `spins` — where a question belongs

sin_python-narrated-command.title: NarratedCommand
sin_python-narrated-command.help: a command named in the third person — `hides()`, `locks_for_night()` — where a call is an order, not a description of one

sin_python-computed-boolean-argument.title: ComputedBooleanArgument
sin_python-computed-boolean-argument.help: a method taking only bools that every caller computes from the same object — the decision re-derived at each call site

sin_python-converted-argument.title: ConvertedArgument
sin_python-converted-argument.help: a scalar parameter its callers keep filling with the same conversion — `receipt_for(str(order.id))` call after call — because it asks for the converted form instead of the value

sin_python-derived-argument.title: DerivedArgument
sin_python-derived-argument.help: a call that hands over an object and a projection of it — `persist(request, request.channel_id)` — or an object in three pieces, where the function could read them itself

sin_python-param-resolved-from-param.title: ParamResolvedFromParam
sin_python-param-resolved-from-param.help: a function that takes a container and a key and first resolves one against the other — `def rename(workflow, node_id)` doing `workflow.graph.node(node_id)` — when it only wanted what the key names

sin_python-repeated-guard.title: RepeatedGuard
sin_python-repeated-guard.help: the same compound `and` condition recurs in 2+ places — it still counts even when reordered, or read through a local variable — and nobody has named it.

sin_python-repeated-named-call.title: RepeatedNamedCall
sin_python-repeated-named-call.help: the same `**changes` call is built the same way with the same keyword at 2+ sites — an operation that has no name on the type it belongs to.

sin_python-repeated-type-guard.title: RepeatedTypeGuard
sin_python-repeated-type-guard.help: the same multi-`isinstance` narrowing (`isinstance(x, A) and isinstance(x.y, B)`) is written in 2+ places — a check on a shape that nobody has named.

sin_python-nullable-registry-lookup.title: NullableRegistryLookup
sin_python-nullable-registry-lookup.help: a keyed store handing back `None` for a key it lacks — `return self._handlers.get(kind)` — so every caller decides what a miss means

sin_python-feature-envy.title: FeatureEnvy
sin_python-feature-envy.help: a method that loops another object's collection or writes its fields, reaching into it more than into its own state — behaviour exiled from the object it works on

sin_python-keyed-lookup-envy.title: KeyedLookupEnvy
sin_python-keyed-lookup-envy.help: a method that uses an object's key to fetch a fact about it through a collaborator — `self.registry.get(node.key).reserved` — treating the object as a key into its own data

sin_python-type-switch.title: TypeSwitch
sin_python-type-switch.help: an `isinstance` ladder over classes the codebase owns — the value is asked what it is so the caller can decide what to do.

sin_python-assembled-template.title: AssembledTemplate
sin_python-assembled-template.help: a multi-line string built as a list of line fragments and `"\n".join(...)`-ed, instead of a triple-quoted f-string that shows its output

sin_python-constant-property.title: ConstantProperty
sin_python-constant-property.help: an `@property` whose body never reads `self` — `return "box"` — a stored value made to look like a computed one.

sin_python-masked-invariant.title: MaskedInvariant
sin_python-masked-invariant.help: a literal answering for the object's own scratch state — `self.period.includes(day) if self.period else False` — where the field is only unset because an operation sets it part-way

sin_python-phantom-nullable.title: PhantomNullable
sin_python-phantom-nullable.help: a field annotated `X | None` that every read assumes is there and none guards — a `None` the design never has

sin_python-placeholder-filled-data.title: PlaceholderFilledData
sin_python-placeholder-filled-data.help: `Card(title=…, body="")` — a dataclass field required as `str` handed the blank to satisfy the signature, a value the type cannot catch

sin_python-scratch-state-restore.title: ScratchStateRestore
sin_python-scratch-state-restore.help: `previous = self.scope … self.scope = previous` — an attribute used as per-call scratch, saved and restored around the call

sin_python-coupled-fields.title: CoupledFields
sin_python-coupled-fields.help: a class whose own fields always travel together — assembled into one value again and again, guarded together, or one copying a sibling field's value — one concept held as several fields.

sin_python-data-clump.title: DataClump
sin_python-data-clump.help: The same three or more scalar parameters (`street: str, city: str, postcode: str`) threaded through functions in two or more classes or modules — one concept with no type of its own.

sin_python-dict-bag.title: DictBag
sin_python-dict-bag.help: A parameter typed as a dict read by string keys — `row["sku"]`, `row.get("quantity")` — a record nobody declared

sin_python-dict-return-bag.title: DictReturnBag
sin_python-dict-return-bag.help: `return {"total": …, "tax": …}` — a record of several fields handed back as a dict its callers read by string key

sin_python-hand-rolled-replace.title: HandRolledReplace
sin_python-hand-rolled-replace.help: `return Order(self.number, self.lines, self.note, "paid")` in a dataclass — every field re-listed to change one

sin_python-mutable-value-object.title: MutableValueObject
sin_python-mutable-value-object.help: a dataclass whose own methods write the fields it was built from after construction — a value that changes under everyone holding it

sin_python-positional-tuple-return.title: PositionalTupleReturn
sin_python-positional-tuple-return.help: `return net, vat, currency` — a bundle of different things the caller must unpack by position, where a reordering breaks silently

sin_python-raw-decoded-return.title: RawDecodedReturn
sin_python-raw-decoded-return.help: `return json.loads(…)` — decoded text from outside handed on as bare dicts and lists, its shape known to no type

sin_defended-certain-field.title: DefendedCertainField
sin_defended-certain-field.help: An `?.` on a field the class declares as always present — a defence against a case the type says cannot happen, so the code doubts something the design already rules out.

sin_falsely-optional-field.title: FalselyOptionalField
sin_falsely-optional-field.help: A field declared optional (`x?: T`, `T | null`) that is initialised where it is declared — it is never absent, and every `?.` and `??` downstream defends a case that cannot happen

sin_duplicate-typescript-function.title: DuplicateFunction
sin_duplicate-typescript-function.help: Copy-pasted code — two+ TypeScript functions (a `function`, a method, a `const` arrow; in a `.ts` module or a component's script) with an identical body, formatting and comments aside

sin_near-duplicate-typescript-function.title: NearDuplicateFunction
sin_near-duplicate-typescript-function.help: A near-copy — two+ TypeScript functions with one control-flow skeleton that differ only in their local names or the literals they use (an endpoint, a key, a label)
